title: Handbook of Narratology
publisher: De Gruyter
notes: Second, fully revised and expanded edition; foundational taxonomy for narratological concepts.

title: Focalization
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Entry first created 2011; cites distinctions among information restriction and focalization patterns.

title: Time
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative time, story/discourse/narrating levels, order, duration, and frequency.

title: Plot
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Plot as arrangement, readerly structuration, and authorial design; includes suspense, surprise, coincidence, and reversal.

title: Space
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative space, story space, setting, and possible/counterfactual worlds.

title: Event and Eventfulness
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Event as change of state; eventfulness as context-dependent relevance, unexpectedness, or unusualness.

title: Character
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Character as a text- or media-based figure in a storyworld; characterization and reader inference.

title: Narrator
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrator, narrative mediation, and narrator-character relations.

title: Speech Representation
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Direct, indirect, and free indirect discourse; representation of thought and consciousness.

title: Unreliability
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narratorial unreliability through misreporting, misinterpretation, misevaluation, or underreporting.

title: Narrative Levels
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Embedded narratives, framing, and relations among diegetic levels.

title: Metalepsis
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative-level boundary transgression; revised entry uploaded July 2016.

title: Metanarration and Metafiction
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Distinguishes narrator's reflection on telling from fiction's reflection on its constructedness.

title: Heteroglossia
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Socially and ideologically differentiated voices; narrator-character speech interference and hybrid discourse.

title: Identity and Narration
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative identity, self-positioning, temporal continuity/change, agency, and social relations.

title: Fictional vs. Factual Narration
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Reviews semantic, syntactic, pragmatic, and narratological approaches to fiction/fact distinctions.

title: Narrative Ethics
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Ethics of the told, the telling, writing/production, and reading/reception.

title: Narrative Empathy
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Empathy, perspective-taking, reader reception, and formal invitations to affect.

title: Cognitive Narratology
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative and mind, storyworld building, mental simulation, and reader inference.

title: Narration in Various Media
publisher: Hamburg University Press / University of Hamburg
notes: Narrative mediation across media and intermediality.

title: Reconsidering the Postmodern: European Literature Beyond Relativism
publisher: Amsterdam University Press
notes: Cross-European case studies and debates on postmodern inheritances, sincerity, neo-realism, engagement, and fiction/nonfiction boundaries.

title: A Poetics of Postmodernism: History, Theory, Fiction
publisher: Routledge
notes: Foundational account of postmodernism, historiographic metafiction, parody, intertextuality, and history/fiction relations.

title: The Autofictional: Approaches, Affordances, Forms
publisher: Palgrave Macmillan
notes: Open-access volume treating autofiction as a contested, flexible aesthetic strategy; includes Martina Wagner-Egelhaaf, 'Of Strange Loops and Real Effects' (DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-78440-9_2).

title: Defining Migration Writing
publisher: De Gruyter
notes: Defines migration writing as a broad constellation; discusses multilingualism, creolization, transnational settings, hybrid forms, and digital communication.

title: Literary Multilingualism: The Babel of Modernity
publisher: Brill
notes: Situates contemporary translingual writing in postcolonial, post-Cold War, migration, exile, and transnational contexts.

title: Transmedial Narratology and Transmedia Storytelling
publisher: Palgrave Macmillan
notes: Distinguishes transmedial narratology (narrative devices across media) from transmedia storytelling (content migrating across media).

title: The Generation of Postmemory
publisher: Duke University Press
notes: Introduces postmemory as mediated, intergenerational relation to traumatic pasts; examines family, photography, and transmission.

title: World War II in Contemporary German and Dutch Fiction: The Generation of Meta-Memory
publisher: Routledge
notes: Comparative study of German, Flemish, and Dutch fiction; analyzes reflexive memory poetics, formal play, heteroglossia, shifting perspective, and fact/fiction mixtures.

title: ‘I think I’m beginning to understand. What I’m writing is an infranovel’: Laurent Binet, HHhH and the problem of ‘writing history’
publisher: Taylor & Francis
notes: Case study of Laurent Binet's HHhH; frame narrative and metanarrative expose research, historical truth claims, and fictionalization ethics.

title: Cli-Fi – Genre of the Twenty-First Century? Narrative Strategies in Contemporary Climate Fiction and Film
container: Green Matters: Ecocultural Functions of Literature, pp. 131–153
publisher: Brill
notes: Identifies formal challenges of climate narratives: scientific knowledge, scale, nonhuman agency, and narrative closure.

title: Narrative Discourse: An Essay in Method
publisher: Cornell University Press
source_type: scholarly monograph; English translation of 'Discours du récit' (1972)
notes: Classic account of narrative order, duration, frequency, mood/focalization, voice, and levels.

title: ‘The Return of the Narrative’: The Call for the Novel / Le retour à la narration : le désir du roman
publisher: Peter Lang
notes: Studies contemporary European novels as hybrid forms that rework realist conventions while retaining traces of postmodern experimentation; publisher page presents chapters on French, German, British, Italian, and other writing.
